question: What is the main purpose of using monitoring gadgets in nursing informatics?

options.A: Bridging patient vital signs and nursing action
options.B: Lowering the cost of hospital building materials
options.D: Eliminating the need for patient medical records

explanation: You've got this! These smart devices take raw patient data and translate it into clear info so you know exactly when and how to care for your patient. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h1)

question: How do automated digital alerts from monitors help you on the ward?

options.A: They stop equipment from breaking down
options.B: They write the patient discharge summary automatically
options.C: They warn the nursing team instantly when readings are abnormal
options.D: They prevent patients from moving around the ward

explanation: Great job! These alerts act like an extra pair of eyes, letting you know right away when a patient's vital signs go outside safe limits so you can act fast. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h1)

question: What does a pulse oximeter actually measure in the body?
explanation: Spot on! The pulse ox is that handy little clip on the finger that estimates how much oxygen your patient's red blood cells are carrying. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h2)

question: A patient has cold hands and their pulse oximeter gives a falsely low reading. What is usually the cause?

options.A: Too much oxygen in the blood
options.B: Poor blood flow to the fingers

explanation: Don't worry, learning this saves you a scare on the ward! Cold hands cause blood vessels to narrow (vasoconstriction), so the sensor struggles to read a good pulse. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of cardiac telemetry on a hospital ward?

options.A: Measuring internal core body temperature continuously
options.B: Sending heart rhythms wirelessly to a central nursing station
options.C: Delivering emergency electric shocks to the chest wall
options.D: Pumping medication directly into the central veins

explanation: You're doing great! Telemetry lets stable patients walk around the ward while their heart rhythm is safely watched from the nurses' station. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why do nurses need to check sticky electrode pads regularly on a heart monitor?

options.A: To get a clear signal and avoid annoying false alarms
options.B: To calculate the exact daily fluid balance
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling cold
options.D: To stop the battery from losing its charge

explanation: Exactly! Loose pads pick up static and trigger false alarms, which stresses the patient and wastes your valuable time. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which of these vital signs is tracked by a standard bedside multi-parameter monitor?
explanation: You got it! Bedside monitors are your best friend for keeping an eye on heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, and how fast the patient is breathing. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h4)

question: An arterial line monitor suddenly shows a weak, flat waveform. What should you check first?

options.C: The expiry date of oral medications
options.D: Kinks or air bubbles in the pressure tubing

explanation: Smart thinking! Physical blockages like a kinked line or tiny air bubble will mess up the pressure reading, so always check the tubing first. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the purpose of early warning scores on modern hospital monitors?

options.A: To calculate the monthly hospital utility bills
options.B: To help nurses spot patients who are getting worse
options.C: To replace the need for physical nursing assessments
options.D: To schedule cleaning staff for patient rooms

explanation: Spot on! Early warning scores add up little vital sign changes so you can catch a deteriorating patient before it turns into an emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h5)

question: How does having integrated patient data change everyday nursing care?

options.A: It removes all documentation responsibilities from nurses
options.B: It shifts care from proactive prevention to reactive rescue
options.C: It helps nurses catch problems early before they become emergencies
options.D: It requires patients to stay completely bedridden

explanation: Brilliant! Catching small negative trends early means you can step in with proactive care instead of scrambling during a sudden crash. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is a major ethical worry when patients are on continuous electronic monitoring?

options.A: Making hospital rooms too bright at night
options.B: Reducing the number of available doctors
options.C: Lowering the electric power consumption of the ward
options.D: Concern over patient privacy and personal space

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! Constant tracking can make patients feel like their personal space and dignity are being invaded. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is keeping digital monitor and telemetry data secure so important?

options.A: To speed up the internet connection in the hospital
options.B: To stop unauthorized people from seeing confidential patient info
options.C: To make the monitor batteries last longer
options.D: To ensure the device screen does not crack

explanation: Exactly! Patient trust is sacred. We must protect digital health records from data breaches to keep patient information safe and legal. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h6)
